name: Cameco Corporation
sector: Energy / Uranium mining & nuclear fuel services
moat_justification: Scarce tier-1 high-grade, low-cost uranium assets (Cigar Lake, McArthur River/Key Lake) that cannot be replicated on any investable timeline, plus a long-term contract book and an integrated fuel-cycle position (fuel services, 49% of Westinghouse) — but Cameco is ultimately a uranium price-taker, its reserves deplete (Cigar Lake ~2036, McArthur River shortly after 2040), and production is concentrated in northern Saskatchewan with Kazakhstan JV exposure.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CAD converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 40-F cover (SEC filing, CIK 1009001): securities registered under Section 12(b) are 'Common Shares, no par value', trading symbol CCJ, listed directly on the New York Stock Exchange — the NYSE security is the common share itself, not an ADS) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 1.79 vs 3-yr median 1.10 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.3% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Tier-1 uranium franchise, moat 6/10, net cash — but the price capitalizes a decade of flawless contract repricing: weighted IRR 5.9%, weighted IV@15 $18.72 vs $81.40, and even the super-bull case (9.0% IRR) clears neither 10% nor 15%; clears 15% only below ~$18.72.
moat_for: World's largest high-grade uranium reserves; tier-1 low-cost assets (Cigar Lake, McArthur River/Key Lake) with decade-plus permitting barriers to any replacement supply
Long-term contract book: five-year average contracted deliveries exceeding 28M lb/yr with floors in the high $70s/lb and escalated ceilings around $160/lb
Integrated nuclear fuel cycle: uranium, conversion/fuel services, and 49% of Westinghouse (AP1000 pipeline of 91 reactor opportunities)
Western supply-security premium as utilities bifurcate away from Russian/Kazakh supply
Net-cash balance sheet (engine: net debt -0.18x normalized OE) funds opportunistic stake increases (Cigar Lake to 57.4% in July 2026)
moat_against: Commodity price-taker: earnings are driven by the uranium price, which Cameco does not control
Finite reserves: Cigar Lake mine life ~2036 (extension work ongoing), McArthur River concludes shortly after 2040
Geographic/operational concentration: Saskatchewan flooding and the McClean Lake mill disruption both hit 2026 operations; Inkai JV is in Kazakhstan
Kazatomprom and new supply can undercut on cost; enrichment/substitution and reactor-policy shifts sit outside Cameco's control
Westinghouse earnings are lumpy and equity-accounted (a ~US$170M Dukovany milestone flattered 2025 and did not recur in 2026)
